To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the introduction of market forces and the fragmentation of the energy markets in the Netherlands and in Europe have drastically changed the climate of investments in the electricity sector, which is now a multi-actor problem.
the market paradigm for electricity networks in the Netherlands has resulted in the creation of new challenges for smart grid investments.

(i) the introduction of market forces has drastically changed the investment climate for the electricity infrastructure; (ii) the upgrading of electricity networks into smart grids has become a multi- actor investment problem that requires a well-designed, well-managed, and well-supported process; and (iii) the realization of smart grid requires public support, as the private sector is not able to overcome the overwhelming uncertainties that smart grid investments entail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of public policy in the development of smart grids in the context of market forces and the need for public support.
the question how smart grids can be developed in a market environment.
the question of how to create the right investment climate for smart grid development, which is a prerequisite for a sustainable energy future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the smart grid development process in China will need to be supported by public policy intervention.
the market paradigm is a powerful tool to improve the functioning of the electricity sector, but it does not automatically lead to an efficient and well-functioning sector.
the introduction of market forces has not been beneficial for smart grid investments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the smart grid is not only a technological challenge but also an institutional challenge.
a smart grid is a complex system with many uncertainties and risks, and that the realization of a smart grid is therefore dependent on a well-designed and managed process.
smart public policy is needed to reduce uncertainties in the smart grid investment process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of market forces into the electricity sector in Europe has created an environment that is very similar to the situation in China.
the Chinese government should be aware of the need for public support in smart grid development, which is not a given in a market-driven environment.
China's electricity sector will need to be prepared for an increasing role of market forces, which will have an impact on the investment climate.
